newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open up slightly on few leads.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open up slightly on few leads.

text.p: The Australian share market opened slightly firmer on Thursday, following Wall Street's modest gain, but otherwise there were few strong leads for investors.
At 10.25 a.m. (0025 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.9 points firmer at 2,264.4.
The June share price index was down two points at 2,262 and at a 2.4 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said early trading was subdued with some residual buying left over from Wednesday propping up blue chip issues which rebounded from a sell-off on Tuesday.

"I don't think there is anything driving the market this morning. The market is up but futures have opened lower this is usually a good indication of either arbitrage or simply a directionless market," a dealer from a Melbourne brokerage said.
The dealer said some analysts believed that Tuesday's strong retail sales figure was an abberation and consequently the market was incorrectly sold that day.
"This may be a factor with some of the blue chip issues that are a few cents up this morning," the dealer said.

Building products company Boral and food group Goodman Fielder were both higher after reporting annual results before the opening. The market was awaiting annual results from miner WMC Ltd which are expected to be announced later in the day.
